context.title: Santa Barbara Independent editorial board — November 3, 2026 California general election endorsements

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: This one can be argued both ways, but when possible, we prefer to err on the side of sanity.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: We wonder just how far that $25 billion will go and how many people will actually be helped, but any response to the state’s housing crisis will require scatter-shot solutions. And this is one.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: We have no reason to question the scientific expertise of Michelson’s institute, but we do know a sweetheart deal when we see one.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: For everyone else, we urge you to vote no on Prop. 39. It is dangerously and sloppily written and purports to solve a problem that simply does not exist.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: But if the devil is in the details, then Prop. 40 needs an exorcist.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: That’s the amount of money they have already spent supporting these two initiatives they hatched as poison pills just in case Prop. 40, the billionaire’s tax, were to succeed.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: We are far from thrilled by the hint of higher taxes, but with the federal government now in full retreat from many of its traditional support roles, local governments will have increasingly rely upon their own local resources to weather the local disasters and health-care shortfalls.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: However high-minded and lofty such efficiency mandates might seem, this is absolutely not the time for voters to meddle.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Prop. 45 is just another one-size-fits-all solution that will not succeed in getting affordable housing built but will definitely succeed in making the coast ugly.

positions.statement: We are supporting Becerra mainly because Hilton is so very much worse.

subject.title: Attorney General of California

positions.statement: Even factoring in for inevitable performative theatrics, Bonta has truly outdone himself keeping the Trump White House in partial check.

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 24

positions.statement: One important step is to send Carbajal back to Congress. He deserves our support.

subject.title: Santa Barbara Mayor

positions.statement: We are endorsing councilmember Eric Friedman — a moderate’s moderate who we believe will bring balance and a spirit of cooperation to the council, something that has long been missing from the present group on the dais.

subject.title: Santa Barbara City Council, District 4

positions.statement: If you live in District 4, we urge a vote for Devon Wardlow.

subject.title: Santa Barbara City Council, District 5

positions.statement: For the three council seats, we are endorsing Devon Wardlow, Gabe Escobedo, and Ian Baucke, three young, smart, wonky progressives all with actual experience in government service.

subject.title: Santa Barbara Unified School District Board, Area 1

positions.statement: The other candidate who intrigues us is Mark Philibosian, mostly because his background is in finance and his wife is a teacher.

subject.title: Santa Barbara Unified School District Board, Area 4

positions.statement: Clearly, one of the two most technically qualified is Valerie Amparan, a charter school mom with loads of nonprofit and corporate experience.

subject.title: Santa Barbara Community College District Board, Area 7

positions.statement: In Area 7, encompassing the Mesa, Hope Ranch, the Upper Westside and Samarkand, we are lucky to have a qualified candidate: Andrea Varon, a teacher and school administrator for 43 years.

subject.title: Allan Hancock Joint Community College District — Measure H (Affordable Higher Education Bond)

positions.statement: Measure H is one of the smartest, best conceived education and economic development bond measures to be put before voters anywhere in Santa Barbara County for eons.
